content: RING1 E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase RING1 is an enzyme in humans encoded by the RING1 gene. This gene is a member of the RING finger family, which encodes proteins characterized by the presence of a RING domain. The RING domain is a zinc-binding motif that is structurally related to the zinc finger domain. The protein product of this gene has the ability to bind DNA and functions as a transcriptional repressor. It is associated with the multimeric polycomb group protein complex. The RING1 protein interacts with polycomb group proteins such as BMI1, EDR1, and CBX4. It colocalizes with these proteins in large nuclear domains. Specifically, RING1 interacts with the CBX4 protein through its glycine-rich C-terminal domain. The RING1 gene is located in the HLA class II region of the genome, where it is contiguous with other RING finger genes, including FABGL and HKE4. RING1 has also been demonstrated to interact with CBX8, BMI1, and RYBP.
